q: How much energy is needed to melt $0.40\,\text{kg}$ of ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ and warm the water that forms to $25\,{}^\circ\text{C}$? Use the values $s = 334\,\text{kJ/kg}$ and $c = 4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}}$.
a: Melting: $Q_1 = sm = 334\,\text{kJ/kg} \cdot 0.40\,\text{kg} = 133.6\,\text{kJ}$. Warming: $Q_2 = cm\Delta T = 4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}} \cdot 0.40\,\text{kg} \cdot 25\,\text{K} = 41.9\,\text{kJ}$. In total $Q = Q_1 + Q_2 = 175.5\,\text{kJ} \approx 1.8 \cdot 10^2\,\text{kJ}$, two significant figures like the mass $0.40\,\text{kg}$.

q: Sauna water is thrown on hot stones. Why do the stones cool down much more when the water vaporises than if it only warmed to $100\,{}^\circ\text{C}$?
a: The water also vaporises, and vaporisation needs energy $Q = rm$, which is about $2260\,\text{kJ/kg}$. This is many times more than heating the water: $1\,\text{kg}$ of water from $20\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ to $100\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ needs only $335\,\text{kJ}$. The energy is taken from the stones, so they cool down.
